concerns: The comparison baseline is trained with ground-truth cross-entropy only, while SWAM receives hard-label knowledge distillation and a teacher-initialized classification head, so the small reported accuracy margins cannot be attributed to the merging mechanism itself [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].

Reported accuracy differences are very small (mean deltas from +0.02 to +0.26 percentage points, with some negative values) and are based on only one to three seeds, providing weak statistical support for the claimed gains [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].

The aggressive-schedule results show losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, and the abstract's claim of matching or exceeding baseline is qualified by minimal losses, leaving the headline benefit dataset-dependent and not clearly established [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0002, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the methodological concept is clearly presented, the empirical evaluation contains critical confounding factors: SWAM was trained with knowledge distillation and teacher-initialized weights while the comparison baseline was not [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037]. With performance margins being very small (often under 0.2%), this training mismatch introduces substantial uncertainty regarding the actual efficacy of the merging algorithm.

Table II presents per-seed top-1 accuracy of the baseline
and SWAM, while Table III summarizes the corresponding
mean differences across seeds. Under the conservative schedule
SWAM matches or surpasses the baseline across all three
datasets and all seeds. The most consistent improvement is on

on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet. These results indicate that
the conservative schedule provides a more stable accuracy-

blocking_reasons: The comparison baseline is trained with ground-truth cross-entropy only, while SWAM receives hard-label knowledge distillation and a teacher-initialized classification head, so the small reported accuracy margins cannot be attributed to the merging mechanism itself [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].

Reported accuracy differences are very small (mean deltas from +0.02 to +0.26 percentage points, with some negative values) and are based on only one to three seeds, providing weak statistical support for the claimed gains [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].

The aggressive-schedule results show losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, and the abstract's claim of matching or exceeding baseline is qualified by minimal losses, leaving the headline benefit dataset-dependent and not clearly established [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0002, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final performance is measured with standard ground-truth classification accuracy and hardware efficiency metrics rather than the saliency or distillation losses used in training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 classification accuracy on held-out test and validation splits, plus FLOPs, throughput, latency, and memory measurements [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0035].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Composite loss combining ground-truth cross-entropy, hard-label knowledge distillation, and KL divergence against block-4 attention rollout [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0021].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Because the full-token baseline does not receive the same knowledge distillation or pre-initialized classification weights during fine-tuning, the reported modest accuracy margins (+0.02% to +0.26%) cannot be cleanly attributed to the SWAM merging mechanism rather than distillation and initialization advantages [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Empirical evaluation tests DeiT-Small on CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100 across 1 to 3 seeds, measuring top-1 accuracy, latency, and FLOPs [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0035]. However, the baseline model was trained purely with ground-truth cross-entropy without knowledge distillation, whereas SWAM was trained using teacher knowledge distillation and initialized classification head weights [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0021, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final model performance is measured via standard ground-truth classification accuracy on evaluation splits rather than learned saliency or distillation loss metrics.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard top-1 classification accuracy on held-out test and validation sets alongside FLOPs and latency measurements [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Composite loss consisting of ground-truth cross-entropy, hard-label knowledge distillation, and KL divergence against block-4 attention rollout [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0021].

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that evaluation is limited to DeiT-Small, that standard full ImageNet-1K was not evaluated due to hardware constraints, and that training recipes differed regarding distillation and head initialization [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].
primary.method_assessment: The architectural mechanisms—modulating candidate merge ranking via exponential maximum saliency penalties and blending tokens via exponential saliency weights—are mathematically formulated [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0018, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0019]. Saliency prediction uses an attention-rollout loss at block 4 and task losses thereafter [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0016, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0021].
primary.quality_rationale: While the methodological concept is clearly presented, the empirical evaluation contains critical confounding factors: SWAM was trained with knowledge distillation and teacher-initialized weights while the comparison baseline was not [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037]. With performance margins being very small (often under 0.2%), this training mismatch introduces substantial uncertainty regarding the actual efficacy of the merging algorithm.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces SWAM (Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging), a token reduction framework for Vision Transformers incorporating multiplicative max-saliency pair scoring and asymmetric saliency-weighted token merging guided by lightweight MLP saliency predictors [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0001, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0007, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0018, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0019].

scholarly_quality.rationale: While the methodological concept is clearly presented, the empirical evaluation contains critical confounding factors: SWAM was trained with knowledge distillation and teacher-initialized weights while the comparison baseline was not [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037]. With performance margins being very small (often under 0.2%), this training mismatch introduces substantial uncertainty regarding the actual efficacy of the merging algorithm.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge that evaluation is limited to DeiT-Small, that standard full ImageNet-1K was not evaluated due to hardware constraints, and that training recipes differed regarding distillation and head initialization [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
